territorial_scope.description: EU-wide directive addressed to Member States, which must transpose it into national law, applying to works protected by national copyright law from 7 June 2021.

evidence.quote: This Directive is addressed to the Member States.

summary.short: Harmonises EU copyright for the digital market: exceptions for text and data mining, teaching and heritage preservation; rules on press publishers' rights, online content-sharing platforms' liability and authors' remuneration and transparency. Member States must transpose by 7 June 2021.
summary.long: Harmonises further EU copyright law for the internal market, covering digital and cross-border uses (Art. 1). Member States must provide exceptions for text and data mining by research organisations and cultural heritage institutions (Art. 3), for text and data mining of lawfully accessible works unless rights are reserved by appropriate means such as machine-readable means (Art. 4), for digital illustration for teaching (Art. 5), and for cultural heritage preservation copies (Art. 6). Title III covers licensing of out-of-commerce works, optional extended collective licensing, a negotiation mechanism for video-on-demand audiovisual works, and copyright-free reproductions of public-domain visual art (Arts 8-14). Article 15 grants press publishers a two-year right for online uses by information society service providers. Article 17 makes online content-sharing service providers liable for unauthorised communications unless they show best efforts, and requires user complaint mechanisms. Articles 18-23 cover appropriate remuneration, transparency, contract adjustment, dispute resolution and revocation for authors and performers. Title V amends Directives 96/9/EC and 2001/29/EC and sets application from 7 June 2021 and transposition provisions.
